questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding MPGN type 1 except:

options.label: A
options.text: Histological there is the proliferation of mesangial cells along with the endocapillary proliferation

options.label: B
options.text: Immunofluorescence study shows mesangial deposits of IgG and C-3

options.label: C
options.text: Electron microscopy shows show dense subendothelial deposits

options.label: D
options.text: Spikes are seen on silver stain

questions.answerText: Spikes are seen on silver stain
questions.solutionHtml:
Spikes are seen on silver stain
  • Spikes are not seen on the silver stain in MPGN type 1.
  • MPGN type 1 is a type of glomerulonephritis characterized by mesangial cell proliferation and endocapillary proliferation.
  • Electron microscopy shows dense subendothelial deposits, which give a tram-track appearance.
  • On silver stain, there is a granular deposition of material, but spikes are not seen.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 559

questions.stem: C-3 nephritic factor is associated with:
questions.solutionHtml:
MPGN Type 2
  • C3 nephritic factor is associated with MPGN Type 2, which is also known as dense deposit disease.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 559

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old male with a history of hepatitis C infection presents with proteinuria, hematuria, and elevated serum creatinine. A renal biopsy is performed, and the image of the same is shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
MPGN
  • The given clinical history and history theological image showing “tram-track appearance” suggests the diagnosis of mesangioproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN).


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 559

questions.stem: In a patient with kidney disease, the presence of a 'tram track appearance' on renal histology is indicative of which specific renal condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
MPGN type 1
  • MPGN type 1 is characterized by the deposition of both immune complexes (usually containing IgG and C3) and complement components within the glomerular basement membrane.
  • The classic histological finding in MPGN type 1 is a tram track appearance, which refers to a double contour or duplication of the glomerular basement membrane, seen on light microscopy.
  • In immunofluorescence (IF) staining, MPGN type 1 typically shows both IgG and C3 deposits.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 559
